text: When you design a REST API, you should follow some best practices to make it easy to use. First, create clear and simple endpoints that describe the resources, such as /users or /orders. Use the correct HTTP methods and return meaningful status codes, like 200 for success or 404 when something is not found. Good documentation is also essential, because developers need to understand how your API works. Finally, always plan for versioning, for example by adding /v1/ to the URL. This way, you can improve your API without breaking existing applications. Following these rules helps other developers work with your API quickly and confidently.
